Heard, learned counsel for the parties.
I.A. No.7101 of 2023 in Cr. Appeal (Sj) No.509 of 2023.

1. Heard, learned counsel for the appellant on the aforesaid I.A. filed for condonation of delay of about 78 days in preferring the instant Cr. Appeal (SJ).
2.
Learned APP for the State has raised no serious objection.
3. Considering the grounds taken in Paras 7 & 8, the prayer for delay in filing the instant Cr. Appeal (SJ)is allowed.
I.A. No.7101 of 2023 is disposed of.

Crl. Appeal (SJ) No.509 of 2023.
4. The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 14 (A) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes under the Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 against the order dated 10.02.2023 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST, Dhanbad in MCA No. 3346/2022 [in connection with Nirsa P.S.
Case no. 277 of 2021, SC /ST case no. 83 of 2022] for the offence under Section 406, 420 and 34 of the I.P.C. and under Section 3(i)(r)(s) of the ST SC [Prevention of Atrocities] Act whereby and where under anticipatory bail application of the appellant has been rejected by the learned court below.

sentences.text: As per the F.I.R. a written report was lodged by the informant against three named accused persons including this appellant, alleging therein that the informant's wife had a Petrol Pump at G.T. road, Nirsa, Dhanbad and the named accused, Nirbhay Kumar Upadhay was the Director of BMIPL which was engaged in mining with his partners, Arnab Dhawan and Sanjeev Singh.

It is alleged that named persons approached his wife for supplying diesel in the mining work of credit and acting on the inducement, the diesel was supplied by the Petrol Pump against which payment through cheques were issued by Nirbhay Kumar Upphadhay in favour of the Petrol Pump which was dishonoured and the informant's wife suffered a loss of more than Rs.31 Lakhs due to dishonour of the cheques.
6. It is submitted by the learned counsel on behalf of the appellant that no overt act has been attributed to the appellant as he has not issued any cheque in favour of the wife of the informant.

It is a purely commercial dispute for which the provisions of SC ST Act will not apply, in view of the ratio laid down Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramawatar v. State of M.P., (2022) 13 SCC 635.
7.

entities.text: Ramawatar v. State of M.P., (2022) 13 SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. for the State has defended the impugned order.
It is submitted that there is direct and specific allegation against him.
8. Considering the submissions made, the prayer made in the instant Criminal Appeal is allowed.

Accordingly, the appellant, above-named is directed to surrender before the learned Trial Court within a period of four weeks and in the event of their arrest or surrender, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Trial Court subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C. and further the appellant will co
-operate with the investigation and will appear under Section 41A Cr.P.C. as and when his presence is required.
9. Appellant is directed to surrender before the learned Court below within three weeks of the order.
10. Accordingly, the instant Criminal Appeal is allowed and the impugned order is set aside.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/Uploaded Sanjeev Kumar Singh @ Sanjeev Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118143390/
